titulo: India wins 2025 Women's Cricket World Cup, defeating South Africa by 52 runs

fuente.nota: Text shortened by removing paragraphs; the sentences are unchanged.

parrafos: India women won the 2025 ICC Women's Cricket World Cup after defeating South Africa women by 52 runs in the final held at DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai on Sunday. The tournament was hosted in India, and this victory marked India's first Women's World Cup title.

South Africa won the toss and elected to bowl first. India scored 298 for 7 in 50 overs, led by Shafali Verma's 87 and Deepti Sharma's 58. Opener Smriti Mandhana supported with a partnership of 100 runs with Verma for the first wicket. For South Africa, Ayabonga Khaka took three wickets, while Nonkululeko Mlaba, Nadine de Klerk, and Chloe Tryon took one each. India's total was the second-highest in a Women's World Cup final.

Chasing 299, South Africa made a steady start, reaching 52 for one in the powerplay. Laura Wolvaardt top-scored with a well paced century (101 off 98 balls), while Annerie Dercksen and Sune Luus contributed 35 and 25 runs respectively. India's bowlers maintained pressure in the middle overs. Deepti Sharma claimed five wickets, and Shafali Verma took two, as South Africa were bowled out for 246 runs.

After the match Shafali Verma said, "I said at the start, that God has sent me here to do something nice, and that reflected today. Very happy that we won and I cannot express it in words. It was difficult but I had confidence in myself - that if I can stay calm, I could achieve everything. My parents, my friends, my brother, everyone supported me and helped me understand how to play." South Africa captain Laura Wolvaardt congratulated India, saying, "I couldn't be prouder of this team. Unfortunately we were outplayed today – India played brilliant cricket. We were hoping for a little more swing early on, and we were in it for a lot of the chase, but just lost too many wickets... [In the field] I was checking that scoreboard and they [India] were tracking for a 350. Our back end was amazing."
titulo_es: India win the 2025 Women's Cricket World Cup after beating South Africa by 52 runs
resumen_es: India's women's team win their first Cricket World Cup on home soil by defeating South Africa in the final in Navi Mumbai, with Shafali Verma and Deepti Sharma as the stars.
nivel_motivo: The general vocabulary is simple; the difficulty lies in cricket jargon (wicket, over, toss), which can be learnt with the glossary: B2 better reflects the language level.

ideas_clave.idea: Playing at home in Navi Mumbai, India beat South Africa by 52 runs in the final and claimed its first ever Women's World Cup.
After being sent in to bat, India posted 298 for 7, thanks mainly to Shafali Verma and Deepti Sharma, the second-highest total ever in a women's final.
South Africa's chase, built around Laura Wolvaardt's century, fell short at 246 as India's bowlers, led by Deepti Sharma with five wickets, kept up the pressure.
Verma credited her self-belief and her family's support, while the South African captain congratulated India, admitted her side had been outplayed and praised her team's fightback.

resumen_modelo: The article reports that India's women's team won the 2025 Cricket World Cup, which it was hosting, by defeating South Africa by 52 runs in the final, thereby securing the country's first title in this competition. Having been put in to bat, India scored 298 runs for seven wickets, largely thanks to Shafali Verma and Deepti Sharma, which represents the second-highest total in a women's final. In reply, South Africa, despite a century from their captain Laura Wolvaardt, were bowled out for 246, as Sharma took five wickets. After the match, Verma attributed her performance to her confidence and to the support of her family, whereas Wolvaardt acknowledged that her side had been outplayed while expressing pride in her players.
